in.other_title: Train a verifier on easy tasks, then use it to supervise the generator on hard tasks
in.rationale: Lightman et al. define ORMs trained on final results and PRMs trained on per-step feedback. Sun et al. train ORMs and PRMs only on labelled easy MATH problems (levels 1-3, including PRM800K data) and use them as evaluators to supervise generators on hard problems by re-ranking or RL.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: outcome- and process-supervised reward models used to supervise generators, extended to training only on easy problems

text: Following Uesato et al. (2022), the authors define outcome-supervised reward models (ORMs) as trained using only the final result of a chain-of-thought, and process-supervised reward models (PRMs) as receiving feedback for each step. They argue process supervision gives more precise feedback by locating errors, is easier for humans to interpret, and more directly rewards following a human-endorsed chain-of-thought, noting that outcome-supervised models can reach correct answers with incorrect reasoning.
title: Outcome-supervised (ORM) vs process-supervised (PRM) reward models
